title: Playing with Ma Rainey, 1927-28
summary: Miller explains he played with Ma Rainey from late 1927 to mid 1928, left her ill in Milwaukee, and had come on the road with a tent show that fell apart.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: What about Ma Rainey? You said you were there when she died, huh?
Yeah. No, I wasn't there when she died. I had been playing with her and I left. When she was taking sick, we left her home, see. And she died about a year after that. Oh, after you left her.
What year was that you were playing at home?

I was in the same year after you had in 1917. And I came on the road with Charlotte Taylor about 27 actually. I played Ma Rainey from say about the last of 27 until about the middle of 28. That's how I figured out clothes I could get through. And she was taking sick on the road in Milwaukee I think it was. And just packed up and she came on home, see. And so we just went on with the show until they broke up. And I went back to Chicago.
You were already living on Chicago before you went on the road with Ma Rainey.

I didn't leave with Ma Rainey. I left with the Browns Madigan's as they call them. The man who was named William McBride. But they called them Miramaker, see. And it wasn't so straight so that they split up people. It wasn't paying the people. It wasn't making the money. So the people just left them.
